jp: 週末[しゅうまつ]{の|no-possessive}予定[よてい]{を|o-object}勝手[かって]に変[か]え{ては|te-wa}いけません{よ|yo-assertion}。
en: You mustn't change the weekend plans on your own.
why: A ban is the て-form plus は plus いけません; ても would mean 'even if', not 'must not'.

jp: 友[とも]だち{と|to-with}会[あ]う約束[やくそく]{を|o-object}破[やぶ]っ{ては|te-wa}いけません。
en: You must not break a promise to meet a friend.
why: Doing the verb is what is banned, so the て-form takes は before いけません.

jp: 明日[あした]{は|wa-topic}友[とも]だち{の|no-possessive}家[いえ]{に|ni-destination}早[はや]く行[い]かなく{ては|te-wa}いけません。
en: Tomorrow I have to go to my friend's house early.
why: なくてはいけません is 'must'; なくても would mean 'need not', and なくたら is not a form.

jp: 彼女[かのじょ]{に|ni-target}すぐ謝[あやま]らなく{ては|te-wa}いけない{と|to-quote}思[おも]います。
en: I think I have to apologize to her right away.
why: 'Must do' is なくてはいけない; なくても reverses it to 'it is fine not to'.

jp: 小[ちい]さなこと{で|de-cause}悩[なや]ん{では|te-wa}いけません。友[とも]だち{と|to-with}話[はな]しましょう。
en: Don't worry over small things. Let's talk with a friend.
why: Telling someone not to do something is the て-form (here で) plus は plus いけません; でも would mean 'even if'.

jp: 相手[あいて]{の|no-possessive}気持[きも]ち{を|o-object}考[かんが]えずに話[はな]し{ては|te-wa}、失礼[しつれい]です{よ|yo-assertion}。
en: Speaking without thinking of the other person's feelings is rude.
why: ては introduces an action that is judged negatively; ても would say 'even if you speak'.

jp: 友[とも]だち{と|to-with}けんか{を|o-object}し{ては|te-wa}いけません{よ|yo-assertion}。
en: You mustn't fight with your friends.
why: A ban uses し plus ては plus いけません; しても would mean 'even if', and plain して cannot take いけません.

jp: 簡単[かんたん]に人[ひと]{を|o-object}信[しん]じ{ては|te-wa}いけない{と|to-quote}思[おも]います。
en: I think you shouldn't trust people so easily.
why: 'Should not do' is the て-form plus は plus いけない.

jp: 友[とも]だち{と|to-with}約束[やくそく]した日[ひ]{に|ni-time}、寝坊[ねぼう]し{ては|te-wa}いけません。
en: You must not oversleep on the day you promised to meet a friend.
why: The banned action is marked by て-form plus は; ても would turn it into 'even if'.

jp: 本当[ほんとう]{の|no-possessive}気持[きも]ち{を|o-object}隠[かく]し{ては|te-wa}いけません{よ|yo-assertion}。
en: You shouldn't hide your true feelings.
why: Advice not to do something takes the て-form plus は plus いけません.
